mainTopic: נדרים 26a: רבא's explanation of the מחלוקת between בית שמאי and בית הלל about a vow that accidentally included one's father, and רב פפא's challenge from רבי עקיבא's rule of נדר שהותר מקצתו הותר כולו
overview: The משנה describes a man who forbade a group of people from eating his figs and then found out that his father was among them. רבא explains exactly where בית שמאי and בית הלל argue. If the man says he would have named the others and said 'father is permitted,' everyone agrees the whole vow falls away. They argue only if he says he would have said 'all of you are forbidden except father.' רבא ties this to the argument between רבי מאיר, who says the first words count, and רבי יוסי, who says the end of the sentence counts. רב פפא then challenges רבא from a משנה about רבי עקיבא's rule that a vow which is partly undone is fully undone. That משנה has one case where everyone becomes permitted and one where only the last person is permitted. רב פפא shows that רבה, who holds the opposite of רבא, can fit both parts. He then grants that רבא can explain the first part, setting up the problem with the last part, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבא defines where בית שמאי and בית הלל really argue
steps.stepSummary: רבא says everyone agrees that if the man would have named the others and said 'father is permitted,' everyone is permitted. The argument is only when he would have said 'all of you are forbidden except father.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Everyone agrees that whenever a person says, 'Had I known my father was among you, I would have said: So-and-so and so-and-so are forbidden and father is permitted,' all of them are permitted. They argue only when he says, 'Had I known my father was among you, I would have said: All of you are forbidden except father.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own explanation of the case in the משנה. He shows which wording everyone agrees on and which wording causes the מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man made a vow by mistake, because he did not know his father was there. If his corrected vow would have used separate names plus 'father is permitted,' all agree the whole vow is cancelled. רבא narrows the מחלוקת to one wording only: 'all of you are forbidden except father.'

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees (both sides of the argument)
Had I known. The wording of someone who made a mistaken vow
So-and-so and so-and-so (naming people one by one)
Except for father
They only argued about…

steps.confusionAlert: Both wordings leave the father out of the vow. The only difference is how the sentence is built: listing names, or saying 'all of you' and then 'except father.' The whole מחלוקת depends on that difference.

phrases.english: They disagree only where one says:
Had I known that father was among you,
"All of you are forbidden except father."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבא's own way of explaining the משנה's מחלוקת, different from the explanation that came just before.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With separate names plus 'father is permitted,' all agree everyone is permitted. The מחלוקת is only about 'all of you are forbidden except father.'

steps.title: בית שמאי follow רבי מאיר: hold on to the first words
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי agree with רבי מאיר that we go by the first thing a person says.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי hold like רבי מאיר, who said: Hold on to the first expression.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind בית שמאי's view in the disputed wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first words were 'all of you are forbidden,' so that is what counts. 'Except father' only takes the father out. It does not change the vow, so the vow stays in force for everyone else.

keyTerms.meaning: They hold like (they agree with)
Grab hold of the first expression; the first words count

phrases.english: who said: Hold on to the first expression.
phrases.notes: So 'all of you are forbidden' is what counts, and 'except father' just leaves the father out.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי סָבְרִי לַהּ כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning for בית שמאי in the case רבא identified.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Following the first expression, the vow on the others stays in force.

steps.title: בית הלל follow רבי יוסי: the end of the sentence counts
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל agree with רבי יוסי that a person is held to how he finishes his words.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל hold like רבי יוסי, who said: A person is held to the end of his words.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind בית הלל's view, the other side of the same argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the ending 'except father' counts, the corrected vow really is different from the vow he made. Part of the vow is cancelled, and a vow that is partly cancelled is fully cancelled. So everyone is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: At the end of his words
A person is held (to his words)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, the מחלוקת between בית שמאי and בית הלל is the same as the מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי: do we go by the first words or the last words?

phrases.english: who said: A person is held to the end of his words.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית הִלֵּל סָבְרִי לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבא's explanation by giving בית הלל's side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Following the end of the words, the vow is partly cancelled, so it is fully cancelled.

steps.title: רב פפא challenges רבא with רבי עקיבא's rule: 'all of you'
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא begins his challenge by quoting a משנה. It explains רבי עקיבא's rule that a vow partly undone is fully undone, using the case of 'all of you.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא raised an objection to רבא: How did רבי עקיבא mean that a vow which was partly undone is fully undone? If one said, 'It is קונם that I will not benefit from all of you,' and one of them was permitted, all of them are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא starts a challenge against רבא by quoting a משנה. This step only sets up the source; the actual point of the challenge comes later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה explains that רבי עקיבא's rule works on a vow said as one group: 'all of you.' If one person in that group becomes permitted, the whole vow falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him (from an earlier source)
A vow that is partly undone is fully undone
A word used to make something forbidden by vow
Benefit

phrases.english: Rav Pappa raised an objection to Rava:
that a vow which was partly undone
"Konam, that I will not benefit from all of you,"
phrases.notes: This is quoted from a משנה later in the מסכת (66a).

phrases.english: if one of them was permitted,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge against רבא's explanation.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that with separately named people plus 'father is permitted,' everyone agrees all are permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה gives two outcomes: one where everyone becomes permitted and one where only the released person is permitted. רב פפא will ask which father-case wording each outcome matches. This works for רבה (step 6) but causes trouble for רבא (step 7 onward).

steps.title: The quoted משנה continues: 'this one and that one'
steps.stepSummary: The quoted משנה continues. When a person names people one by one, the result depends on which person becomes permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said, 'That I will not benefit from this one or from that one': if the first was permitted, all are permitted. If the last was permitted, the last is permitted and all the others are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה that רב פפא is using. This sets up the point of his challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the people are listed one by one, the vow is not one single unit. If the first person is permitted, the whole vow falls. If only the last person is permitted, he alone is free and the others stay forbidden. The next steps match these two outcomes (everyone permitted, or only one permitted) to the two wordings from the father case.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one (naming people one by one)
The first one
The last one

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. 'All of you' is one vow, so one release frees everyone. 'This one and that one' is a list, so the outcome depends on whether the first or the last person was released.

phrases.english: "That I will not benefit from this one or from that one,"
if the first was permitted, all are permitted;
the last is permitted and all the others are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes quoting the source of רב פפא's challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that a vow listing names with 'father is permitted' leaves everyone permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה has a first part where everyone becomes permitted and a last part where only one person is permitted. Each part has to be matched to a father-case wording. רב פפא will show that רבה can do this (step 6) but רבא has trouble with the last part (step 7 onward).

steps.title: According to רבה, both parts of the משנה fit
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא shows that רבה can explain the first part of the משנה as a case of 'this one and that one,' and the last part as a case of 'all of you.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for רבה. He explains the first part as a case where the person said 'this one and that one.' He explains the last part as a case where the person said 'all of you.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא is setting up his challenge to רבא. First he shows how smoothly the משנה fits the view of a different אמורא, רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה holds the opposite of רבא. In his view, everyone agrees about 'all of you are forbidden except father,' and the argument is about 'this one and that one are forbidden, and father is permitted.' So in the first part of the משנה, where everyone becomes permitted, the person named people one by one, and the ruling follows בית הלל. In the last part, where only one person is permitted, he said 'all of you,' and everyone agrees.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well for... (it is understandable according to...)
He sets it up as / explains it as the case of...
The first part of the משנה
The last part of the משנה
An אמורא whose view on this question is the opposite of רָבָא's

steps.confusionAlert: רַבָּה (spelled with a ה at the end) is a different person from רָבָא (spelled with an א), whose view we saw in step 1. רב פפא is comparing the two of them.

phrases.english: he sets up the first part
phrases.notes: This is the first part of the משנה from step 4, where everyone ends up permitted.

phrases.english: as a case where he said 'this one and that one.'
And the last part is where he said 'all of you.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the משנה quoted in steps 4-5 and shows it fits רבה's view smoothly.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first half of a 'this works for him, but not for you' argument: it shows the משנה fits רבה perfectly, which will make the gap in רבא's view stand out.

steps.title: According to רבא, the first part fits
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא turns to רבא and grants that the first part of the משנה can be explained as a case of 'all of you.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to you: it works for the first part, since you can explain it as a case where he said 'all of you.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא now speaks to רבא directly. He agrees that רבא can explain the first part of the משנה, and this sets up the problem with the last part, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, the argument is about 'all of you are forbidden except father,' and בית הלל say everyone becomes permitted. So the first part of the משנה, where everyone is permitted, fits as an 'all of you' case that follows בית הלל. The phrase 'it works for the first part' hints that the last part will be a problem for רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: But (turning to the other side)
According to you

steps.whyThisMatters: This 'it works for him, but for you...' structure is how the גמרא builds a challenge. Once it grants that the first part fits, the reader should expect trouble with the second part.

phrases.notes: רב פפא is now talking directly to רבא.

phrases.english: it works for the first part; you set it up
as a case where he said 'all of you.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבה's smooth reading to רבא's reading, granting the first part as a setup for the challenge on the last part.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the argument is only about 'all of you are forbidden except father'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבא uses the 'all of you' case for the first part, where everyone is permitted, then he will have trouble explaining the last part, where only one person is permitted.
